findings.description: storage_encrypted is set to false, so the RDS MySQL instance and its underlying storage/snapshots are stored unencrypted, exposing database contents if the underlying storage or a snapshot is accessed.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint (also exported via the db_endpoint output), placing a production-style database directly on the internet where only the security group stands between it and untrusted networks.

findings.issue_category: database credentials from variable / default admin user
findings.description: The master username is the predictable 'admin' and the password is supplied via var.password, which in this repository pattern is a plaintext Terraform variable that also ends up in state and in EC2 user data; no Secrets Manager / managed master password is used.

No enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports (audit/error/general/slowquery) are configured and IAM database authentication is disabled, so authentication and query activity against a publicly reachable database cannot be reviewed after a compromise.

The MySQL parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the publicly accessible database accepts unencrypted client connections, allowing credentials and query data to traverse the network in cleartext.

The RDS security group is defined without any restriction and is paired with an egress rule allowing all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted outbound path usable for data exfiltration or C2.
Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, removing any outbound network boundary and enabling exfiltration from a compromised database host.

The inline role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". Because this role is attached via the instance profile to an internet-facing web instance, any compromise of the web app yields full control of all S3 data, EC2, and RDS in the account, including privilege escalation paths such as modifying instances and snapshots.

The user_data script interpolates the database username and var.password into a PHP include file; EC2 user data is stored unencrypted and retrievable from the instance metadata service (and from Terraform state), leaking the RDS master credentials.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains available; combined with a PHP web application and an over-privileged instance profile, a simple SSRF gives an attacker account-wide credentials.
No root_block_device / ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance's volumes (which contain the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file) are stored unencrypted.

The bootstrap installs httpd serving the credential-handling PHP application over plain HTTP with no TLS, and the instance's public DNS is exported, so form submissions and session data traverse the network in cleartext.
